source.title: LAUNDRY-SERVICE-001: co-optimize washer-to-dryer performance, textile life and lifecycle burden
source.body:
## Objective

Create an evidence-bounded, end-to-end benchmark for the **laundry service delivered by a washer + dryer pair**, integrating existing washer architecture and appliance morphology work without creating a second appliance lifecycle, repair, provenance or safety subsystem.

The functional unit is: `1 kg of dry-equivalent textile accepted after a declared wash/rinse/dry process`. Acceptance requires the declared textile/load to meet preregistered cleaning, rinse-residue, fabric-care and final-moisture floors. Energy, water, detergent, elapsed time, textile wear, microfiber release, service cost and downtime are reported as a vector; no single weighted score may hide a failed hard gate.

## Why this is new work

Existing #1825/#1828 establish a service-first washer study; #1893 includes the hypothesis of washer-spin moisture + dryer moisture/energy coordination. This issue turns that cross-appliance hypothesis into a measurable whole-service protocol and explicitly adds textile life, microfiber mass balance, and the heat-pump dryer's own service/performance trade-offs. It composes with—not replaces—those owners.

## Research basis and measurement standards

- Washer performance: IEC 60456:2024 (Edition 6), including cleaning performance, rinse performance, fabric gentleness and load-related methods.
- Tumble-dryer performance: IEC 61121 (published edition and national adoption to be confirmed at protocol freeze).
- Washer-dryer combinations, if later included: IEC 62512 / applicable EN IEC 62512 edition.
- Safety is separate: IEC 60335-2-7:2024 (washing machines), IEC 60335-2-11:2024 (tumble dryers, including heat-pump and flammable-refrigerant provisions), plus applicable South African SANS/NRCS/VC 9008 requirements and product-market conformity routes.
- Dryer fire-risk research: IEC TS 63576:2025, used only within its defined scope.
- Desk-researched commercial references are not selected controls; exact product code/revision, market test basis and program equivalence must be frozen before ranking.

## Work

1. Freeze a comparable washer and dryer control set (at least three comparable model families per appliance class where feasible); document exact product code/revision/market, capacity, cycle/program, label method, manuals, dated price, repair documentation and known caveats.
2. Define a matched wash-to-dry workload: textile mix, dry-equivalent mass, soil/stain challenge, water hardness, detergent/dose, ambient conditions, wash program, spin, transfer delay, dryer program and final moisture endpoint.
3. Measure washer cleaning, rinse residue, fabric gentleness, residual moisture after spin, energy, water, detergent, cycle time and noise.
4. Measure dryer inlet/outlet moisture, moisture removed, electricity, elapsed time, condensation efficiency, exhaust/condensate, airflow restriction, lint/filter maintenance burden and noise.
5. Measure complete-pair energy, water, detergent, time and cost per kg of accepted dry-equivalent textile. Keep washer-only, dryer-only and paired totals separately reportable.
6. Add repeated-cycle textile wear and microfiber mass-balance measurements. Distinguish fiber captured from fiber released; account for filter bypass, retained mass, cleaning loss, sludge and uncertainty.
7. Compare service access and repairability using existing washer and appliance-repair task graphs; do not duplicate Mycelix work orders or part-provenance identities.
8. Evaluate heat-pump dryer air-side service cassettes, lint/heat-exchanger fouling, moisture sensing, low-temperature operation, airflow feedback, desiccant/hybrid concepts and thermal recovery as separate hypotheses.
9. Test washer spin extraction vs downstream dryer energy/time as a joint Pareto trade: higher spin speed is not automatically better if fabric wear, vibration, noise, unbalance or lifecycle cost worsens.
10. Establish a South African household deployment profile: local supply voltage/frequency, water pressure/quality/hardness, tariffs, service/parts lead times, ambient conditions and outage / backup-power scenarios. Confirm exact SANS/NRCS scope before design freeze.

## Proposed targets — research hypotheses only

- Washer desk reference: 10 kg AEG LR9WW80409 publicly listed at 20 kWh/100 Eco cycles and 50 L/cycle; a third-party energy-label dataset reports 235 min, 53.9% residual moisture and 72 dB. Market/method comparability must be checked before physical controls are selected.
- Dryer desk reference: 8 kg AEG TR948V4BC publicly listed at 73 kWh/100 cycles (0.73 kWh/cycle), 94% condensation efficiency and 60 dB; the official AEG Ireland listing for PNC 916 900 129 gives 3h19 full-load and 2h05 half-load durations. Confirm exact product number/market/program and test method before comparison.
- Washer ambition against the 10 kg reference: ≤18 kWh/100 matched cycles and ≤45 L/cycle as first differentiation hypotheses; stretch ≤16 kWh/100 and ≤42.5 L/cycle. Require cleaning/rinse/gentleness non-inferiority under a frozen IEC 60456:2024-compatible method.
- Spin extraction: residual moisture ≤50% initial hypothesis; ≤45% stretch, only if fabric gentleness, vibration, noise, balance and service life remain within frozen limits.
- Dryer ambition against the 8 kg reference: ≤0.62 kWh/cycle first target; ≤0.55 kWh/cycle stretch, at matched load and final moisture. Weighted duration ≤145 min first target and full-load ≤180 min stretch, without sacrificing fabric protection or condensation efficiency; target ≥96% condensation efficiency and ≤58 dB as proposed values.
- Microfiber capture: ≥80% by mass within the declared capture boundary as a stretch research target; a 2025 study of three commercial filtration systems reports 35–65% capture and a hydraulic-performance trade-off, with full mass balance and pressure-drop / bypass / clogging / maintenance measurements. This is not an assumed filter result.
- Repairability: preserve #1828 hypotheses (≥25% lower median and P90 verified restoration time; ≥90% completion of approved user-maintenance tasks) and add dryer air-side service tasks.
- Whole-life economics: target ≥15 years of documented parts/service support as a design ambition and explore ≥20% lower lifecycle cost per 1,000 kg of accepted output against matched controls. Do not claim this from short accelerated tests or nominal prices.
- Targets are not results; do not freeze superiority thresholds until control-only repeatability, measurement uncertainty, workload and non-inferiority margins are established.

## Paradigm shifts

- Product pair -> whole laundry service: optimize accepted clean, rinsed, fabric-preserved, dried textile rather than advertised cycle.
- Washer and dryer silos -> upstream/downstream co-optimization: residual moisture after spin is a measured dryer input; optimize the combined Pareto frontier.
- Energy label -> multi-output evidence: cleaning, rinse, fabric gentleness, final moisture, microfibers, time, noise, durability, repair cost and resource use.
- Fixed programmes -> quality-constrained adaptive process: choose the lowest-resource sequence that meets declared outcome floors; abstain when sensors or input conditions are out of scope.
- App/cloud dependency -> offline-first service: essential controls, maintenance and diagnostics function locally.
- Proprietary fault codes -> observable, repairable product: distinguish command, sensor observation, hypothesis, intervention and verified restoration.
- Disposable filter -> measured microfiber containment: report captured/released mass and maintenance burden.
- One factory -> qualified local manufacture/repair: stable interfaces and public technical files; no unqualified physical interchangeability claims.

## System ownership and composition

- Symtropy: physical/process design-space, thermal/air/water/energy balances, architecture trade-offs and benchmark protocol. Its current rigid-body engine must not be misrepresented as validated CFD/psychrometric simulation; extend required models explicitly and validate against measurements.
- Symthaea: advisory load/process optimization and next-test selection using existing EIG/EVSI; measure value over fixed-rule and conventional adaptive baselines via ablation. No safety actuation or interlock authority.
- Mycelix: reuse exact-unit, BOM, part, work-order, supplier and repair-evidence owners (including existing RepairProductiveLoop / physical-product evidence work); no duplicate ledger.
- Sol-Atlas: consume qualified lifecycle, household-cost, access and repair knowledge as read-only projections; do not create a competing source of truth.
- Physical safety: independent deterministic protective controls and qualified review. Model outputs never override interlocks, over-temperature protection, door locks, leakage protection or guarded rotating mechanisms.

## Benchmark and evidence rules

- At least three comparable controls per appliance class where feasible; freeze model, market, program and workload. Set unit/technician sample size by pilot variance and the target claim, not by an arbitrary minimum alone.
- Publish the protocol and analysis plan before candidate measurements; include calibrated instrumentation and uncertainty.
- Keep synthetic, simulation, desk-researched, bench-measured, field-observed and independently replicated evidence classes distinct.
- No energy/water superiority claim if cleaning/rinse/fabric/final-moisture floors fail.
- No life, reliability, fire safety, water hygiene, electrical safety or conformity claim from simulation or one-off demonstrations.
- Unknown costs, missing data and censored follow-up are not zero or success.
- Safety, functional output, textile damage and unacceptable environmental discharge are non-compensatory gates.
- Compare distributions and uncertainty; use Pareto/robust dominance, not an arbitrary weighted composite.

## Initial acceptance criteria

- [ ] Washer-to-dryer benchmark document and machine-readable profile with explicit claim ceiling.
- [ ] Separate washer, dryer and paired functional units and denominators.
- [ ] At least 12 metric definitions with unit, method, evidence class, uncertainty and guardrail.
- [ ] Positive and negative controls for unmatching capacity/program, bypassed microfiber mass, unknown inputs, quality-floor failure and model-overrides-interlock attempts.
- [ ] Existing Symtropy owners reused; no duplicate repair/provenance/EVSI/safety subsystem.
- [ ] First physical experiment chosen by expected decision value and low risk; no powered prototype work before safety and design review.
- [ ] Exact-head formatting/tests/audit and digest-bound receipt before any contract PASS claim.

## Nonclaims

No washer/dryer has been built, purchased, physically tested, safety-qualified, independently replicated or shown to outperform the market by this issue. All numeric goals above are hypotheses. Public product listings are sourcing leads, not selected controls or independently reproduced measurements.


## Competitive intelligence update — 16 November 2026

The original desk-reference set should be expanded to include current feature-rich bubble/AI washers, not only energy-label and local-market models. These are sourcing and control candidates, not selected physical controls:

- **Samsung WW12BB944DGMNQ (Africa-market page):** AI Wash and AI Ecobubble are listed. Samsung describes sensing load weight, fabric softness and soil level, then adapting water, detergent, soak, rinse and spin times. The manufacturer states AI Ecobubble activates only on certain programmes and loads below 2 kg. Its advertised 24% more soil removal / 70% energy saving comparison is explicitly based on IEC 60456:2010, 4 kg, cold Super Eco versus Cotton 40°C on two different legacy models; it is not a matched modern-method comparator. Product page: https://www.samsung.com/africa_en/washers-and-dryers/washing-machines/ww9400b-front-loading-ai-ecobubble-ai-wash-bespoke-design-with-space-max-12kg-white-ww12bb944dgmnq/
- **Samsung WW11CGC04DABFA (South African product page):** 11 kg Eco Bubble model. The page's feature note says the Less Microfiber cycle is not available on the SSA model. Do not transfer features from another regional variant to the locally specified SKU. Product page: https://www.samsung.com/za/washers-and-dryers/washing-machines/ww5000c-front-loading-eco-bubble-smartthings-ai-energy-mode-less-microfiber-cycle-11kg-black-ww11cgc04dabfa/
- **Toshiba T25-series UFB (2025 catalogue):** the catalogue describes 10^6/ml ultra-fine bubbles and markets energy/time/water savings. Its published 82% energy / 19% time / 6% water figures compare a Cotton cycle against a Color Alive cycle; that comparison does not isolate UFB as the causal factor and must not be treated as independent matched-control SOTA. Catalogue copy: https://device.report/m/7b7a68e165331861b8b80b89028d09370a90fc2c2957892e1764a4b8e4436404

### Consequence for our differentiation

Do not position "bubble washing", "AI wash optimization", "microfiber cycle" or local manufacture as an invention. Competitors already offer versions of these features. The differentiation hypothesis is:

1. Physically characterize the treatment medium (size/concentration/dissolved-gas/time stability) rather than adopting vendor bubble labels.
2. Show net energy/water/detergent benefit at matched accepted cleaning, rinsing and fabric-care outcome using a modern frozen protocol, not dissimilar programme labels or legacy cross-model comparisons.
3. Co-optimize washer spin and dryer energy/time without accepting excessive textile wear, vibration or noise.
4. Close the microfiber mass balance across washer drain, bypass, dryer lint/air path, condensate and filter-cleaning waste while monitoring hydraulic performance.
5. Publish uncertainty, negative results, calibration, exact model/market/program and maintenance effects. Symthaea's contribution must be measured against fixed-rule, random and conventional DOE baselines.

### Control selection consequences

Add Samsung's AI Wash/EcoBubble feature-rich model family to the desk-review cohort, and Toshiba UFB as a feature-claim comparator. They remain **desk references only** until exact regional SKU, product revision, official energy/water fiche, manual, cycle definitions, part/service support and physical availability are verified. Before any ranking, choose at least three physically obtainable control model families per appliance class and run the same frozen workload. Never rank a 2010-method manufacturer claim against a 2024-method test result.


## Additional paradigm shift — garment surface and chemistry (16 November 2026)

A new workstream [GARMENT-SURFACE-001 #5527](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symtropy/issues/5527) investigates interventions upstream of the appliance:

- A 2026 *Communications Chemistry* paper reports a PDADMAC/PVS hydration-layer coating with water-rinse self-cleaning on its tested fabrics, performance beyond 100 laundering cycles and an approximately 82% resource reduction in the paper's compared process. These are laboratory findings, not proof of full-garment wearability, skin safety, breathability, coating-retention, end-of-life or recyclability. Reference: https://www.nature.com/articles/s42004-026-01942-7
- A 2025 multi-institution study reports lower fibre-fragment mass with a purpose-formulated low-shed detergent, including a full garment wash-plus-dry study. This needs matched cleaning/rinse tests and whole-path mass balance before adoption. Reference: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.clema.2025.100303
- A 2025 plasma-jet stain study reports improvement for several stains on white cotton but weaker oil removal, with reactive species generation. It remains a shielded professional-lab pretreatment hypothesis, not a household process. Reference: https://doi.org/10.1080/09593330.2025.2530029

This broadens the system goal: design the garment, chemistry and care equipment together. A textile treatment is only an improvement if coating release, skin contact, comfort, breathability, durability, repairability, recycling and wastewater fate remain acceptable.
